folders.name: Photo analysis (macOS)
folders.what: What macOS works out from the photos and videos in your library: what's in them, for search, Visual Look Up and the text in images.
folders.grows: It analyses each new photo and video, and may go through the whole library again after a macOS update; what it keeps grows while it works.
folders.helps: Leave it to macOS: deleted, it would analyse the whole library again, which takes hours. It does most of its work while the Mac is plugged in and idle.

folders.name: Photo analysis (macOS)
folders.what: What Photos works out about your library: the people, places and moments it groups into Memories and People & Pets.
folders.grows: It looks at each new photo and video, and may go through the whole library again after a macOS update.
folders.helps: Leave it to macOS: deleted, it would look through the whole library again. It does most of its work while the Mac is plugged in and idle.

folders.name: Voice Memos
folders.what: Your Voice Memos recordings.
folders.helps: Recordings you delete stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days, unless Voice Memos' Settings clear them sooner.

folders.name: Safari
folders.what: Safari's cache and what websites store in it: their data, databases and offline copies.
folders.grows: Websites store more as you visit them, and the cache keeps copies of their pages and media.
folders.helps: Safari → Settings → Privacy → Manage Website Data… removes what sites stored; with Settings → Advanced → Show features for web developers on, Develop → Empty Caches empties the cache.

folders.name: Slack
folders.what: Slack's data: its cache, the files and images you opened, and each workspace's local copy.
folders.helps: Help → Troubleshooting → Clear Cache and Restart empties its cache.

folders.name: Maps data (macOS)
folders.what: Map data macOS downloaded for Maps and for apps that show maps.
folders.helps: It's a cache: Maps downloads again what it needs.

folders.name: iCloud Drive
folders.note: Downloaded iCloud files: Remove Download keeps them in iCloud only

folders.name: OneDrive
folders.note: OneDrive's copy of what it keeps on this Mac

folders.name: Docker
folders.note: Docker's disk image: `docker system prune` frees what no container uses
folders.what: Docker Desktop's disk image: every image, container, volume and build cache is in this one file.
folders.grows: It grows as images are pulled or built and as containers write. What Docker deletes goes back to macOS a few seconds later.
folders.helps: Remove the images and containers you no longer use (`docker system prune` removes what nothing uses, never volumes); Docker Desktop's Settings → Resources sets how big the disk image may get.

folders.name: Android SDK
folders.what: What Android Studio downloaded: SDK platforms, build tools and the emulators' system images.
folders.helps: Android Studio's SDK Manager removes the platforms and system images you no longer build for.

folders.name: Gradle
folders.what: Gradle's caches: the dependencies and Gradle versions your projects' builds downloaded.
folders.grows: Each new dependency version, and each Gradle version a project's wrapper asks for, adds to it.
folders.helps: Gradle deletes what no build used for 30 days by itself.

folders.name: Cargo
folders.what: Cargo's downloads: the source of each crate version and git dependency your builds used.
folders.helps: Since Rust 1.88, Cargo deletes by itself what no build used for months.

folders.name: Rust toolchains
folders.what: The Rust toolchains rustup installed: stable, nightly and each version a project pins.
folders.helps: `rustup toolchain list` shows them; `rustup toolchain uninstall <name>` removes one you no longer use.

folders.name: Flutter versions
folders.what: The Flutter SDKs fvm installed, one for each version a project pins.
folders.helps: `fvm list` shows them; `fvm remove <version>` removes one.

folders.name: npm
folders.what: npm's cache: each package version npm downloaded, for any project.
folders.grows: npm doesn't delete old versions by itself.
folders.helps: `npm cache clean --force` empties it; installs download again what they need.

folders.name: pnpm
folders.what: pnpm's store: one copy of each package version, shared by all projects.
folders.helps: `pnpm store prune` removes the versions no project uses.

folders.name: Dart packages
folders.what: Pub's cache: each Dart and Flutter package version your projects used.
folders.helps: `dart pub cache clean` empties it; projects download again what they need.

folders.what: bun's cache: each package version bun downloaded.
folders.helps: `bun pm cache rm` empties it; installs download again what they need.

folders.what: pip's downloads, and the wheels it built.
folders.helps: `pip cache purge` empties it.

folders.what: Go's module cache: each module version your builds downloaded.
folders.helps: `go clean -modcache` empties it; builds download again what they need.

folders.name: Simulator devices
folders.note: Simulators' apps and data: `xcrun simctl delete unavailable` removes those of runtimes that are gone
folders.grows: Each simulator keeps the apps you ran in it and their data, and the simulators of runtimes you removed stay behind.

folders.name: Xcode DerivedData
folders.what: Xcode's build output, indexes and logs, a folder for each project it built.
folders.grows: Each build adds to its project's folder, and the folders of projects you no longer open stay.
folders.helps: It can be deleted while Xcode isn't building: the next build makes what it needs again.

folders.name: Xcode archives
folders.what: Each build you archived to upload or export, with its debug symbols.
folders.helps: Xcode's Organizer deletes old archives; keep those of versions whose crash reports you still read.

folders.what: What Xcode copies from each iPhone or iPad it runs apps on, once for each iOS version.
folders.grows: A new copy, often several GB, for each iOS version a device you connected ran.
folders.helps: The folders of versions your devices no longer run can be deleted; Xcode copies one again when it needs it.

folders.name: App search index
folders.note: Spotlight's index of what's in your apps
Downloaded cloud files: Free Up Space keeps them in the cloud only

folders.what: Chrome's profiles (history, extensions, what websites stored) and the data of Google's other apps.
folders.grows: Websites store more as you visit them; Chrome also downloads an on-device AI model of a few GB when its AI features are on.
folders.helps: In Chrome, Settings → Privacy and security → Delete browsing data removes what sites stored.

folders.what: Chrome's cache: copies of pages and media, to load them faster again.
folders.helps: Chrome deletes from it as it fills; Delete browsing data → Cached images and files empties it.

folders.what: VS Code's data: its settings, each folder's workspace storage, extensions' data, and its caches.
folders.helps: Its caches (Cache, CachedData, Code Cache) can be deleted while VS Code is closed; it makes them again.

folders.what: Comet's data (Perplexity's browser): its profiles, what websites stored, and its caches.
macOS's record of how you use the Mac, for Siri Suggestions, Screen Time and the like; it stays on this Mac.
folders.helps: Leave it to macOS, which trims it by itself.

folders.what: The private folders of macOS's background services, each named by an id instead of the service.
folders.helps: Leave them to macOS.

folders.what: Python packages installed for your account (`pip install --user`), and their commands.
folders.helps: `pip list --user` lists them; `pip uninstall <name>` removes one.

folders.what: The browsers Playwright downloaded to run tests: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, for each Playwright version.
folders.grows: Each Playwright version needs its own browsers; Playwright deletes a version's once nothing on this Mac uses it.
folders.helps: `npx playwright uninstall --all` removes them all; tests download them again.

folders.what: The Windows SDK and C runtime cargo-xwin downloaded to build Rust for Windows.
folders.helps: It can be deleted: cargo-xwin downloads it again for the next Windows build.

folders.what: Homebrew's downloads: the bottles and sources of what it installed.
folders.helps: `brew cleanup` deletes old downloads, which Homebrew also does by itself every 30 days.

folders.what: Swift Package Manager's cache: the packages it downloaded, for any project.
folders.helps: `swift package purge-cache` empties it; builds download again what they need.

folders.what: The Dart analysis server's cache, for Dart and Flutter in VS Code and Android Studio: what it worked out about each package it analysed.
folders.grows: It adds to it for each package and Dart version it analyses, and doesn't delete old ones.
folders.helps: It can be deleted while no editor is open: the analysis server makes what it needs again.

folders.what: Claude Code's data: each session's transcript, its plugins and settings.
folders.grows: Every session adds its transcript; Claude Code deletes those older than 30 days by itself.
folders.helps: `cleanupPeriodDays` in ~/.claude/settings.json keeps transcripts for fewer days.

folders.what: bun: the program, the packages installed with `bun add -g`, and its package cache (install/cache), mostly the cache.
folders.helps: `bun pm cache rm` empties the cache; installs download again what they need.

folders.what: Where command-line tools put what they install for you: programs in .local/bin, their data in .local/share (uv's Pythons, pipx's apps).

folders.name: System downloads
folders.note: Voices, dictionaries and models macOS downloads

folders.name: Document versions
folders.what: The versions macOS keeps of documents as apps save them: what File → Revert To lists.

folders.name: Homebrew
folders.note: What Homebrew installed. It removes old versions by itself every 30 days, so this is what's installed now: `brew leaves` lists what you asked for, and `brew uninstall` removes one

folders.name: Sleep image
folders.note: Where the Mac keeps memory while it sleeps
folders.grows: Swap files are added when apps need more memory than the Mac has; they go when the Mac restarts.

folders.name: Command Line Tools
folders.what: Apple's command-line developer tools (compilers, git, the macOS SDKs), for builds outside Xcode; Homebrew needs them.
Temporary files programs put here.
folders.helps: macOS deletes them when the Mac restarts, and those unused for 3 days.

folders.what: Command-line tools and libraries installed outside macOS: Homebrew on Intel Macs, and installers like TeX's, Python's or the AWS CLI's.
folders.helps: Each came from an installer you ran; its uninstaller, or `brew uninstall`, removes it.

folders.what: macOS's own records: the system log (diagnostics, uuidtext), install receipts, and its services' databases.
folders.grows: The log keeps the last days' or weeks' messages, up to a size macOS sets.
folders.helps: Leave it to macOS: it trims the log by itself, and only macOS changes these folders.

folders.what: What apps installed for every account on the Mac: drivers, plug-ins, sound and media libraries, licences.
folders.helps: An app's folder here goes with the app: its uninstaller removes it.

folders.what: Sounds and plug-ins for audio apps: Apple Loops, sound libraries and Audio Units plug-ins.
Microsoft AutoUpdate's downloads: the Office and Teams updates it fetched to install.
